title: When the eyes close, the lid tears along a hard vertical seam at the eye corners (moon on every blink and the final sleep; sun mid-blink)
owner: src/render/faces.ts (lidMap() and the lid remap at :232-244); src/config.ts (EYES region, if a taper width is added)
evidence: [eyes-poem] Area: src/render/faces.ts:232-244 (open = lo - up; travel = shut * open; p.y = y - travel above the band), seen at 1920x1080 on the bottom (moon) and top (sun) eyes. Checked at 1:1 and zoomed. Moon: at the full-closure frames of every moon blink sampled (t 27.10, 30.76, 36.87-36.93, 41.10, 46.35), both outer ends show a straight vertical cut about 100 px tall. Lashes outside the cut stay up; inside it, the lash band slides down, with stretched 1-px streaks along the cut (screen x about 297 on the left eye, about 1600 on the right). It stays on screen through the final sleep (48.3, 48.6) until the curtains cover it. Sun mid-blink (t 34.0, 42.85): the lash band moves down as a block with vertical sides and a black slot above it. Files: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ayush-Video-claude-Code-Sun-and-Moon/002feb2e-6b4d-4dca-83e5-825de1bd59b7/scratchpad/review4/eyes-poem/corner_zoom.png (3x zoom, open vs shut), /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ayush-Video-claude-Code-Sun-and-Moon/002feb2e-6b4d-4dca-83e5-825de1bd59b7/scratchpad/review4/eyes-poem/blink_left.png, /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ayush-Video-claude-Code-Sun-and-Moon/002feb2e-6b4d-4dca-83e5-825de1bd59b7/scratchpad/review4/eyes-poem/lids_moon.png, /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ayush-Video-claude-Code-Sun-and-Moon/002feb2e-6b4d-4dca-83e5-825de1bd59b7/scratchpad/review4/eyes-poem/lids_sun.png, /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ayush-Video-claude-Code-Sun-and-Moon/002feb2e-6b4d-4dca-83e5-825de1bd59b7/scratchpad/review4/eyes-poem/blink_strip.jpg (30 fps, 36.77-37.13). Cause given by the lens: each picture column slides by travel = shut*(lo-up) at that column; at the blunt temple ends the lid opening (lo - up) goes from 0 to tens of px within a few columns, so neighbouring columns slide by very different amounts and the lash band shears into a vertical seam. The earlier eyes check (moon blink 30.55-30.92, 'no slit') looked for slits, not this shear.
fix: Make the slide vary smoothly across x. Option 1: put a horizontally smoothed opening in a second pair of channels of lidMap(), e.g. a running max or a wide Gaussian of (lower - upper) along x, tapered to 0 over about 25-40 picture px from each tip; use it for the band/lash translation (travel_band = shut * openSmooth) and keep the real edge (up + shut*open) for where the eye is covered, so the lid still lands on the lower lid. Option 2: extend each eye's remap range past the tips over the outer lash flick, with travel fading to 0 there, so the outer lashes bend down instead of being cut. Re-check with a 30 fps strip zoomed 3x at both corners for moon 36.77-37.13, sun 33.84-34.12, and the final sleep at 48.0-49.0.

title: 'Press Enter to restart' stays on screen through the whole replay if the viewer restarts or scrubs back within 0.4 s of the end
evidence: [code, high] src/ui/ui.ts:75-78 (setReplay), :22 (later); 52.0-52.4 s, any screen size. setReplay(true) starts a 0.4 s timer (UI.replayDelaySeconds) that is never cancelled; setReplay(false) only removes the class, so the pending timer adds it back. Playwright at 1280x720: loaded ?t=51.3, waited for state.ended, pressed R straight away, waited 1.5 s: {t: 1.475, ended: false, replayOn: true, opacity: '1'}. Screenshot /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ayush-Video-claude-Code-Sun-and-Moon/002feb2e-6b4d-4dca-83e5-825de1bd59b7/scratchpad/review4/code/A_restart_race.png shows the prompt over the closed curtains of the restarted story. Nothing hides it again until the next end, so it stays over the dialogue and the poem for 52 s. Space, Enter, R or a tap in the first 0.4 s after the end all trigger it; a returning visitor pressing Enter as soon as the curtains meet is the likely case. [robustness, medium] Reproduced: seek to 51.8, wait for state.ended, press R; 1.2 s later t=1.21, playing, .sm-replay has is-on, opacity 0.855. ArrowLeft held across the end (scrubbing) or a fast Enter/Space hit the same window. Output: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ayush-Video-claude-Code-Sun-and-Moon/002feb2e-6b4d-4dca-83e5-825de1bd59b7/scratchpad/review4/robustness/keys-end.out (line 'restart within 0.4s of end, +1.2s'). Repro: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ayush-Video-claude-Code-Sun-and-Moon/002feb2e-6b4d-4dca-83e5-825de1bd59b7/scratchpad/review4/robustness/keys-end.mjs
fix: Keep the timer id and cancel it. In ui.ts: let replayTimer = 0; setReplay(on) { clearTimeout(replayTimer); if (on) replayTimer = window.setTimeout(() => show(replay, true), UI.replayDelaySeconds * 1000); else show(replay, false); }. Also clear replayTimer in dispose(). (Both lenses proposed the same fix.)

Crop: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ayush-Video-claude-Code-Sun-and-Moon/002feb2e-6b4d-4dca-83e5-825de1bd59b7/scratchpad/review4/robustness/fout/fout-crop.jpg. [code, medium] src/main.ts (boot, no preload); src/render/poem.ts:89-105 (layout measures at first landing); src/render/dialogue.ts:100-131; stale comment src/config.ts:710 'Canvas fonts (loaded in main.ts)'. main.ts only imports the @fontsource CSS; the only explicit load is the curtains title (TITLE_FONT). title: The sound plays about 80-140 ms behind the picture because the audio output delay is never accounted for
owner: src/soundtrack.ts (:21 latencyHint, :58/:64 offset and start, :80 drift check); src/main.ts (time passed to soundtrack.update)
evidence: [robustness] Affects the whole film, in the dialogue subtitles and the poem's words. Measured by tracking every AudioBufferSourceNode.start together with ctx.getOutputTimestamp(). Scheduled position was -0.003 to -0.049 s against the story clock, so the code's own check (SOUND.syncTolerance 0.08) passes. Audible position was -0.08 to -0.139 s, because ctx.outputLatency is 0.072-0.08 s and baseLatency 0.021 s here and none is compensated. The schedule also starts from the frame's timestamp (frameT), about 17 ms older than the moment the clip is scheduled. Outputs: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ayush-Video-claude-Code-Sun-and-Moon/002feb2e-6b4d-4dca-83e5-825de1bd59b7/scratchpad/review4/robustness/audio-sync.out ('driftHeard' values) and /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ayush-Video-claude-Code-Sun-and-Moon/002feb2e-6b4d-4dca-83e5-825de1bd59b7/scratchpad/review4/robustness/keys-end.out (-0.139 just after the click at t≈5). On Bluetooth headphones outputLatency is often 150-250 ms.
fix: In start(), schedule from what will be heard: const lag = ctx.outputLatency || ctx.baseLatency || 0; const offset = t + lag - TL.audio[clip]. In update(), compare against t + lag the same way. Pass a fresh time to soundtrack.update (clock.now(performance.now()) instead of the frame's timestamp). Use latencyHint 'interactive' (or a number such as 0.02) to reduce buffering delay.

title: Pausing while the WebGL context is lost leaves the sound playing
evidence: [robustness] Rare: only during a GPU reset or driver crash. soundtrack.update() runs only inside requestAnimationFrame, and drawing stops while the context is lost. After loseContext(), pressing Space gives clock.paused=true, but the poem source is still live with a drift of 0.812 s 0.8 s later; it stops only when the context is restored. If the context never returns, the voice plays on over a frozen 'paused' story. Output: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ayush-Video-claude-Code-Sun-and-Moon/002feb2e-6b4d-4dca-83e5-825de1bd59b7/scratchpad/review4/robustness/ctxloss.out. Repro: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ayush-Video-claude-Code-Sun-and-Moon/002feb2e-6b4d-4dca-83e5-825de1bd59b7/scratchpad/review4/robustness/ctxloss.mjs
fix: At the end of command() in main.ts, after any clock change, call soundtrack.update(clock.now(now), !clock.paused && !clock.now(now) >= TIMELINE.end), so the audio follows input even when no frames are drawn (fix text as given by the lens). Alternatively, keep a light timer for sound updates while contextLost is true.

title: Restoring the WebGL context while a resize is pending logs 25 WebGL warnings
owner: src/main.ts (resize handling :116-120, webglcontextrestored :176); src/render/stage.ts (Stage.resize / composer targets)
evidence: [robustness] Happens after a context restore that follows a window resize made while the context was lost. Lose the context, resize 2560x1080 -> 1920x1080, restore: 25 copies of 'WebGL: INVALID_OPERATION: delete: object does not belong to this context' (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-ayush-Video-claude-Code-Sun-and-Moon/002feb2e-6b4d-4dca-83e5-825de1bd59b7/scratchpad/review4/robustness/resize-ctx.out). title: Shader undefined behaviour: division by zero in the sun's eye flare, and reversed smoothstep edges
owner: src/render/faces.ts (:311 flare, :249, :302), src/render/stage.ts (:119), src/render/curtains.ts (more reversed smoothsteps); src/config.ts (:415 EYES.glow.rays.sun) for context
evidence: [code] For the sun's eyes ray.x = 0 (EYES.glow.rays.sun = [0, 1, 0], config.ts:415), so `o.x / (ray.x * ir.z)` divides by zero and gives 0/0 on the column or row where p is exactly on the iris centre; the result is then multiplied by ray.z = 0. GLSL ES calls this undefined. Tested the exact expression on this GPU (Chrome, ANGLE-GL, Radeon) with o.x=0, o.y=0 and both >0: no NaN or Inf in any case, so it does not explain the HANDOFF's 1-px green/red column here (see F6). A GPU whose max() propagates NaN would draw a NaN line through the sun's irises. smoothstep(e0, e1, x) with e0 > e1 is also undefined in the GLSL ES 3.0 spec (stage.ts:119, faces.ts:249, :302, and more in curtains.ts), although ANGLE and desktop drivers compute the plain formula.
fix: faces.ts:311: skip the flare when ray.z == 0 (`float flare = ray.z > 0.0 ? ... : 0.0;`) or divide by `max(ray.x * ir.z, 1e-3)`. Write the reversed ramps as `1.0 - smoothstep(-w, w, x)` (stage.ts:119), `1.0 - smoothstep(0.85, 1.0, f)` (faces.ts:249) and `1.0 - smoothstep(lo - uFeather, lo, p.y)` (faces.ts:302), and likewise in curtains.ts.

title: Tunables hard-coded outside config.ts, including a 16 px root font size that can misplace the calm patch
owner: src/render/curtains.ts (:1600, :1614, :1621), src/render/poem.ts (:709), src/ui/ui.ts, src/ui/ui.css (:164-168), src/config.ts (CURTAINS.calm at :634, CURTAINS and POEM regions)
evidence: [code] src/render/curtains.ts:1621 (const rem = 16), :1614 (flicker rates 7.3 / 12.9 and weights 0.6 / 0.4), :1600 (valance 0.62); src/render/poem.ts:709 (poem fades in over reveal 0..0.6); src/ui/ui.css:164-168 (18vh and the font clamp, duplicated in CURTAINS.calm at config.ts:634). The calm patch and print-free patch under the prompt are computed in JS from CURTAINS.calm assuming 1rem = 16 px, while the button is sized by CSS rem; if the browser default font size is not 16 px (accessibility setting), the button moves/resizes but the patch does not. The 18% position and font clamp live in two places (ui.css and config.ts), so changing one silently breaks the other. curtains.ts line numbers are moving because another agent is editing it.
fix: In curtains.ts use `const rem = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).fontSize) || 16;`. In ui.ts set `--sm-replay-bottom` and `--sm-replay-font` from CURTAINS.calm, the same way fade timings are already passed, and use those variables in ui.css. Move the flicker rates, the 0.62 swag depth and the poem's 0.6 reveal fade into the CURTAINS and POEM regions.

title: shots.mjs exits 0 when the page throws, fails to boot or logs GL errors
evidence: [code] Problems (console errors and warnings, pageerror, boot error) are collected and printed, but the process still exits 0. verify.mjs runs it through execFileSync, which only fails on non-zero exit, so `npm run verify` reports success over broken frames.
